decision_conditions: The development to which this permission relates must be commenced not later than three years from the date of this permission.
Reason:-
To comply with the requirements of Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended by Section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004).
The development hereby permitted shall not be carried out otherwise than in complete accordance with the approved plans (as set out on page one of this decision notice).
Reason:-
For the avoidance of doubt and to ensure that the development is carried out as approved.

No above-ground works shall take place until details of all external facing materials (including bricks, roof tiles, and window/door frames) have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall be constructed strictly in accordance with the approved details.
Reason:-

To ensure the visual appearance of the building is sympathetic to the surrounding character and local vernacular, in accordance with Havering Local Plan Policy 26, London Plan Policy D4, and the National Planning Policy Framework (2026).

Prior to the commencement of development, a comprehensive scheme of hard and soft landscaping including the retention and protection measures for the mature western boundary trees during construction, details of native tree and shrub planting, boundary treatments, and a 5-year post-planting maintenance schedule shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. All landscaping shall be carried out in strict accordance with the approved details during the first planting season following the substantial completion of the development.
Reason:-

To safeguard existing trees, enhance the visual amenity and environmental quality of the site, preserve the openness of the Green Belt, and secure biodiversity benefits in accordance with Havering Local Plan Policies 27 and 29, London Plan Policy G1, and the National Planning Policy Framework (2026).

Prior to the first occupation of the development hereby approved, the 18 car parking spaces (including 1 accessible bay and active/passive electric vehicle charging infrastructure) shown on the approved plans shall be constructed, made fully operational, and permanently retained thereafter for the parking of vehicles in connection with the development.
Reason:-

To ensure that adequate car parking provision is made off street, and provide infrastructure for electric vehicles in accordance with Havering Local Plan Policy 24, London Plan Policy T6, and the National Planning Policy Framework (2026).

Prior to the commencement of the development hereby approved, details of all proposed walls, fences and boundary treatment shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority.  The boundary development shall then be carried out in accordance with the approved details and retained permanently thereafter to the satisfaction of the Local Planning Authority.
Reason:
To protect the visual amenities of the development and prevent undue overlooking of adjoining property.

Prior to the first occupation of the development, details of the design, capacity, and siting of secure refuse and recycling storage facilities shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The storage facilities shall be provided in accordance with the approved details prior to first occupation and retained permanently thereafter..
Reason:-
To protect the amenity of occupiers of the development and also the locality generally.

No building shall be occupied or use commenced until cycle storage is provided in accordance with details previously submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The cycle storage shall be permanently retained thereafter.
Reason:-

Insufficient information has been supplied with the application to demonstrate what facilities will be available for cycle parking.  Submission of this detail prior to occupation in the case of new building works or prior to the use commencing in the case of changes of use is in the interests of providing a wide range of facilities for non-motor car residents and sustainability.

All building operations in connection with the construction of external walls, roof, and foundations; site excavation or other external site works; works involving the use of plant or machinery; the erection of scaffolding; the delivery of materials; the removal of materials and spoil from the site, and the playing of amplified music shall only take place between the hours of 8.00am and 6.00pm Monday to Friday, and between 8.00am and 1.00pm on Saturdays and not at all on Sundays and Bank Holidays/Public Holidays.
Reason:-
To protect residential amenity.

No loading, unloading, external storage activities, movement of goods, operation of plant or equipment, or other activities within the external yard area shall take place except between the hours of 07:00 and 19:00 Monday to Friday, 08:00 and 13:00 on Saturdays, and at no time on Sundays or Bank Holidays.

Furthermore, any external security or operational lighting installed on the site shall be fully shielded and directed downwards to prevent light spill beyond the site boundary and into the surrounding Green Belt.
Reason:-

To protect the living conditions and residential amenity of nearby occupiers (such as Knoll Cottage) and safeguard openness of the Green Belt, in accordance with Havering Local Plan Policy 7, London Plan Policy D3, and the National Planning Policy Framework (2026).

Prior to the first occupation of the development hereby approved, a scheme of biodiversity enhancements including details of the permanent integration of a minimum of two bird nesting boxes (swift bricks) within the external elevations of the new building and native wildlife-friendly planting shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The approved ecological features shall be installed in full prior to the first use of the building and permanently retained thereafter.
Reason:-

To secure positive environmental enhancements, support local nature recovery, and provide nesting habitats for priority species in accordance with Havering Local Plan Policy 30, London Plan Policy G1, and the National Planning Policy Framework (2026).

Prior to the commencement of development, details of a sustainable surface water drainage scheme (SuDS) utilising permeable paving or soakaways for all new hardstanding areas shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The approved drainage system shall be fully implemented prior to the first occupation of the building and maintained for the lifetime of the development.
Reason:-

To prevent an increased risk of flooding, improve water quality, and properly manage surface water runoff in accordance with Havering Local Plan Policy 32, London Plan Policy SI 13, and the National Planning Policy Framework (2026).
No delivery, service, or commercial transport vehicles exceeding 8 metres in length shall enter, manoeuvre within, or service the application site at any time.

Reason: In the interests of highway safety, traffic flow, and to ensure that large vehicles can safely enter and exit the site in forward gear without causing obstruction on the adjacent high-speed dual carriageway (A127), in accordance with Havering Local Plan Policies 23 and 24, London Plan Policy T4, and the National Planning Policy Framework (2026).
1)No plant or machinery shall be installed unless it meets, or mitigation is employed, to meet the following standard:

The Rating Level (Lar, Tr) of the hereby permitted plant or machinery shall be at least 10dB below the prevailing background noise level (LA90, T).  The measurement position, assessment and definitions shall be made according to BS4142:2014 + A1:2019 "Methods for rating and assessing industrial and commercial sound."
The equipment shall be maintained thereafter to the satisfaction of the Local Planning Authority, and the use hereby permitted must cease during any period that this condition is not complied with.
Reason:   To protect the amenity of noise sensitive premises from noise from mechanical plant.
1)Prior to the commencement of any works pursuant to this permission the developer shall submit for the written approval of the Local Planning Authority;

a)            A Phase I (Desktop Study) Report documenting the history of the site, its surrounding area and the likelihood of contaminant/s, their type and extent incorporating a Site Conceptual Model.

b) A Phase II (Site Investigation) Report if the Phase I Report confirms the possibility of a significant risk to any sensitive receptors.  This is an intrusive site investigation including factors such as chemical testing, quantitative risk assessment and a description of the sites ground conditions.  An updated Site
Conceptual Model should be included showing all the potential pollutant linkages and an assessment of risk to identified receptors.

The Demolition/Construction Method statement shall include details of:
1.	The site access point(s) of all vehicles to the site during the demolition/construction    phase
2.	parking of vehicles of site personnel and visitors;
3.	storage of plant and materials;
4.	Wheel washing facilities.
5.	Measures to monitor and control the emission of dust and dirt during construction.
6.	measures for minimising the impact of noise and, if appropriate, vibration arising from construction activities;
7.	predicted noise and, if appropriate, vibration levels for construction using methodologies and at points agreed with the Local Planning Authority;

Prior to the commencement of the development hereby approved, an Air Quality Neutral Assessment shall be submitted to and agreed by the Local Planning Authority. The assessment must comply with London Air Quality Neutral guidance and updated guidance, at the time the report is submitted.The assessment shall detail;
·	Calculations of the predicted building emissions and comparison against the Building Emission Benchmarks;
·	Calculations of the predicted transport emissions and comparison against the Transport Emission Benchmarks;
·	Mitigation (if required) or contribution to off-setting the development's emissions, taking into account the most up to date Defra's damage costs and relevant guidance on offsetting payments.

The use hereby permitted shall not commence until all measures identified in the Air Quality Neutral Assessment have been shown to be implemented to the satisfaction of the Local Planning Authority in writing.

Within 3 months of first occupation, a Post-Installation Noise Verification Report shall be submitted demonstrating that the development complies with the approved Noise Impact Assessment and required mitigation.
Reason:-
To ensure the approved noise mitigation measures are effective and continue to safeguard residential amenity, in accordance with Policies 7 and 34 of the Local Plan.

The external yard area shown on the approved plans shall be used solely for purposes ancillary and incidental to the approved office use of the site and shall not be used as a separate storage, distribution, open yard, contractor's yard, waste transfer, or other independent commercial operation.
Reason:-

To safeguard the amenities of neighbouring occupiers and to ensure that the use of the site remains compatible with the character of the area, in accordance with Policies 7 and 34 of the Havering Local Plan and the National Planning Policy Framework.

All external storage associated with the development shall be confined to the designated yard area shown on the approved plans. No materials, equipment, goods, containers, plant or machinery shall be stored elsewhere within the site. The height of any external storage shall not exceed 3 metres above surrounding ground level at any time.
Reason:-

To ensure a satisfactory appearance of the development and to safeguard the character of the area and the amenities of neighbouring occupiers, in accordance with Policies 7, 26 and 34 of the Havering Local Plan and the National Planning Policy Framework.

Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (as amended), or any Order revoking and re-enacting that Order, the building shall only be used for purposes falling within Schedule 2, Part A, Class E(g)(i) (Offices to carry out operational or administrative functions)  Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987 (as amended) and for no other purpose, including any other purpose within Class E of the Schedule to the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987 (as amended).
Reason:-

To ensure that the premises remain compatible with the surrounding Metropolitan Green Belt location, maintain adequate parking and highway safety standards on the adjacent strategic transport network (A127), and safeguard the living conditions of nearby residential occupiers, in accordance with Policies 7, 23, and 34 of the Havering Local Plan.

The application property is within the Metropolitan Green Belt where there are restrictions over development.  In view of the approved development, it should not be assumed that further extensions will be agreed.
Changes to the public highway (including permanent or temporary access)

- Planning approval does not constitute approval for changes to the public highway. Highway Authority approval will only be given after suitable details have been submitted considered and agreed. If new or amended access is required (whether temporary or permanent), there may be a requirement for the diversion or protection of third party utility plant or highway authority assets and it is recommended that early involvement with the relevant statutory undertaker takes place. The applicant should email environmentbusinesssupport@havering.gov.uk for further information. Please note that unauthorised work on the highway is an offence.
